findings.title: Preserve the blocked verifier exclusion during environment retries

gold.summary: Legacy adoption trusts Git administration paths selected by an agent-controlled checkout.

findings.title: Include worktrees created before their path was persisted
findings.detail: The migration only checks state.worktreePath. Prepare creates the worktree before its first state checkpoint containing that path. If the previous daemon stopped during that interval, the linked worktree exists but persisted state still has phase "prepare" and no worktreePath. This guard skips recording it, then createWorktree's reuse branch immediately calls worktreeGit and fails with "Missing trusted Git paths". This legitimate upgrade-resume case remains broken.
findings.failure_scenario: Before #323, a run creates its linked worktree, then the daemon stops before prepare persists worktreePath. After upgrading, the scheduler resumes that run with phase "prepare", an existing worktree, and no .git-paths record.

gold.summary: A fixed review-time cutoff excludes worktrees created before the sidecar-writing release actually started.

findings.title: Do not use the commit timestamp as the installation upgrade boundary
findings.detail: An installation can continue running the release without sidecars after this timestamp. Its worktrees remain legacy, but this migration excludes them permanently, so resume still fails with Missing trusted Git paths. Targeted command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-dQbGth/claude-501/legacy-review.ts cutoff`. Output: `cutoff: hasLegacyWorktree = false`, followed by `AssertionError: Old-release worktree must be eligible for recovery` and `false !== true`.
findings.failure_scenario: The previous release successfully prepares a worktree at timestamp 1791100000000, parks the run, and upgrades afterward. The worktree has no sidecar but is excluded from legacy recovery.

findings.title: Recognize interrupted preparation before any gate event
findings.detail: Preparation creates the worktree and saves worktreePath before running the baseline. Shutdown during the first baseline command can leave a cancelled prepare stage without any gate event. Even before the cutoff, this legitimate legacy worktree fails both eligibility conditions. Targeted command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-dQbGth/claude-501/legacy-review.ts interrupted`. Output: `interrupted: hasLegacyWorktree = false`, followed by `AssertionError: Old-release worktree must be eligible for recovery` and `false !== true`.
findings.failure_scenario: An old daemon shuts down after saving worktreePath while the first baseline command is running, with an immediately available gate slot. After upgrading, resume cannot register the worktree.

findings.title: Support legacy worktrees attached to local source repositories
findings.detail: The engine always supplies cachePath, and registration additionally requires a bare owner. Existing code explicitly supports older local worktrees attached directly to their source repository; these cannot pass either restriction. Targeted command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-dQbGth/claude-501/legacy-review.ts local`. Output: `factory-cache registration: Unsafe worktree Git administration`, `source-owner registration: Unsafe worktree Git administration`, then `AssertionError: Legacy local-source worktrees must be recoverable`.
findings.failure_scenario: A migration-eligible local run has a missing sidecar and administration under `<repo.localPath>/.git/worktrees/`. Resume searches the factory cache instead; supplying the actual source owner also fails the bare assertion.

gold.summary: Arbitrary assertion text mentioning a timeout is classified as a transient CI failure.

findings.title: Suppressed PR failures are never reconsidered when main recovers
findings.detail: Main-red classification returns true and clears ciPending. Subsequent polls invoke classification only after the PR's CI changes. findings.failure_scenario: A PR job times out while main's same check is red. Main subsequently becomes green, but the PR remains unchanged and failed. Every subsequent poll skips classification indefinitely.

findings.title: Main-red failures bypass the job logs needed for ledger signatures
findings.detail: This branch records the failure and continues before fetching the Actions job or logs. Normal Actions checks often have empty output, so distinct failures collapse into a conclusion-only signature with no runner image. Running `bun /private/tmp/lr-mb3Cm4/claude-501/review-ci.ts` produced a ledger row with line "timed_out", image null, and no job or log requests.
findings.failure_scenario: Main and a PR both fail a check named test. The PR logs contain the failing test and runner image, but its check output is empty. The ledger records only ["test","timed_out",null], losing the requested failure identity and image.

gold.summary: A definitively refused CI rerun remains pending indefinitely.

findings.title: A CI inspection error prevents later PRs from being observed
findings.detail: Classifier errors propagate through record() and abort the repository's observation loop. A persistent error on the first PR therefore prevents subsequent PR snapshots and feed events from being saved, even though GraphQL returned them successfully. Command: `TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review.test.ts"`. The unavailable-log fixture produced `later PR: {"saved":null,...}` and failed with `expect(received).not.toBeNull(); Received: null` after two polling cycles.
findings.failure_scenario: The first tracked PR has a failed Actions job whose logs endpoint repeatedly returns 404. A second PR in the same repository remains unobserved on every polling cycle.

findings.title: A definitively rejected rerun remains pending forever
findings.detail: The ledger claim is persisted before POST, but every non-201 response throws without resolving the claim. If GitHub rejects the request with 422, no later run attempt exists. Subsequent inspections keep the entry pending and suppress ci.needs_fix indefinitely. Command: `TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review.test.ts"`. The fixture reported `{"outcome":"rerun_requested","needsFix":0,"pending":true,...}` and failed with `Expected length: 1; Received length: 0`.
findings.failure_scenario: A timed-out job qualifies for a rerun, but POST actions/jobs/21/rerun returns HTTP 422. The workflow stays on attempt 1 and classification never completes.

findings.title: Case-sensitive repository URLs reject valid GitHub jobs
findings.detail: Repository resolution preserves user-supplied slug casing, while GitHub returns canonical casing in check_run_url. This exact string comparison rejects a valid job; rerun reconciliation has the same problem at line 258. Command: `TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review.test.ts"`. With stored slug o/r and canonical URLs O/R, the fixture reported `{"reruns":0,"errors":["GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Incomplete failing job"]}` and failed with `Expected length: 1; Received length: 0`.
findings.failure_scenario: A repository is registered as mattflower/limitless, but GitHub returns check URLs containing MattFlower/limitless. Transient failures cannot rerun or finish classification.

findings.title: Definitively rejected reruns remain pending forever
findings.detail: The rerun is claimed before the POST, but a definitive rejection such as HTTP 422 only throws. The ledger remains rerun_requested. findings.failure_scenario: A transient job failure qualifies for rerunning, but GitHub returns HTTP 422 without starting another attempt. Every later inspection leaves the failure pending and emits no actionable classification.

gold.summary: Rate-limit refusals leave rerun claims unresolved across cooldowns and restarts.
ANSI-colored Bun failures and pytest security failures are missed by the retry exclusion.

findings.title: Recognize Node test-runner timeout diagnostics
findings.detail: The timeout matcher rejects Node's actual diagnostic, `error: 'test timed out after 10ms'`, so an eligible test timeout emits ci.needs_fix without rerunning. A fixture using captured Node TAP output with GitHub-style timestamps reproduces this. Command: `bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review.test.ts"`. Output: `Node timeout {"reruns":0,"needsFix":1}`; assertion: `Expected length: 1; Received length: 0`.
findings.failure_scenario: A factory PR's Actions job finishes with conclusion failure because a Node test exceeds its own timeout; main is green and reruns are enabled.

findings.title: Resolve rerun claims rejected by rate limiting
findings.detail: The claim is persisted before POST, but a rate-limit response leaves it permanently rerun_requested. Subsequent inspections wait for a newer workflow attempt that was never started, suppressing both another request and ci.needs_fix. Command: `bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review.test.ts"`. After ten polls following HTTP 429 with Retry-After: 2, output was `rejected POST {"postCount":1,"outcome":"rerun_requested","needsFix":0,"restCalls":80}`; assertion: `Expected: true; Received: false`.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub rejects the first rerun POST with HTTP 429. The cooldown expires, but the originating workflow remains at its original attempt because no rerun was accepted.

findings.title: Record failures in the ledger during main-red pauses
findings.detail: The main-red branch continues before job/log inspection and recordCiFailure, so these failures never enter the ledger. Pausing per-PR reactions should not discard the requested failure history. Command: `bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review.test.ts"`. Output: `main red {"ledger":0,"mainRed":1}`; assertion: `Expected length: 1; Received length: 0`.
findings.failure_scenario: Main and a factory PR fail the same non-security check. If the PR subsequently advances to another SHA before main recovers, its original failure is permanently absent from the ledger.

findings.title: Active fix rounds still appear as awaiting review

findings.detail: The process line splitter drops empty lines, so assembling callbacks with newlines cannot reconstruct credentials containing blank lines. findings.detail: Redaction recognizes JSON-escaped variants, but the truncation overlap uses only literal credential lengths. An escaped multiline credential is longer; if the runner cuts its prefix, removing the literal-length overlap leaves its suffix exposed. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-gate-redaction.test.ts". findings.detail: Replacing the 8,000-character per-line cap with full-line retention removes the character bound on the diagnostic window. The final excerpt budget does not constrain memory retained while a gate runs. Additional lines also join and copy the entire window. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-gate-redaction.test.ts". The bounded-memory assertion failed with Expected: < 1000000; Received: 39000000 after observing 39 million-character lines.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate emits 39 very large diagnostic lines without a recognized result boundary. The shared daemon retains all their contents; increasing line sizes can exhaust memory.

findings.title: Recover legacy worktrees before their path is persisted
findings.detail: Recovery only examines ctx.state.worktreePath. During preparation, createWorktree creates the checkout before that path is persisted. gold.summary: Arbitrary assertion text mentioning a timeout is classified as a transient CI failure.

Output: Expected: "failed_then_passed"; Received: "rerun_requested". The confirmed-rerun control passed.

findings.title: Resume suppressed PR inspection when main recovers
findings.detail: Main-red suppression completes inspection and clears ciPending. Subsequent unchanged PR snapshots never inspect main again, so recovery of the default branch cannot resume the suppressed reaction. Even another PR updating the repository's main-red state does not schedule this PR. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-poller-review.test.ts". The recovery probe output was: Expected length: 1; Received length: 0.

findings.title: Isolate CI inspection errors to the affected PR
findings.detail: An exception from classifyCi propagates out of record and aborts the repository's entire observation loop. Because tracked PRs have stable ordering and failed inspections remain pending, a persistent detail failure on the first PR repeatedly prevents later PRs from being observed, including merge and closure changes. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-poller-review.test.ts". Output: "GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Incomplete CI log" twice; the assertion that PR 2 had saved observation data failed with Received: null.

findings.title: Reconcile rerun requests whose POST response was lost
findings.detail: Only rows marked rerunning are reconciled. If GitHub accepts the POST but its response is lost, the persisted row remains rerun_requested. Running `bun run "$TMPDIR/ci-review.ts"` produced: `lost POST response then passing rerun: expected failed_then_passed; actual rerun_requested`.
findings.failure_scenario: GitHub accepts a job rerun, the connection drops before its 201 response reaches the poller, and the rerun passes at the same SHA.

findings.title: Find the rerun job across workflow attempts
findings.detail: Reconciliation searches only the workflow's latest attempt. Attempt-specific job lists can omit jobs rerun in an earlier attempt. If another job is subsequently rerun, the original job has zero matches and classification throws indefinitely, leaving its ledger outcome unresolved. Running `bun run "$TMPDIR/ci-review.ts"` produced: `origin rerun completed in attempt 2; unrelated job rerun created attempt 3: actual Error: Ambiguous CI rerun job ledger rerunning`.
findings.failure_scenario: The factory reruns job A in attempt 2. Before the next poll, another job in the workflow is rerun in attempt 3. Attempt 3's job list excludes A.

findings.title: Deduplicate main-red notifications at repository scope

findings.failure_scenario: Both build and test fail on main and on a factory PR. The classifier emits two ci.main_red feed items.

findings.title: One CI inspection error starves other PRs in the repository

The failing PR retains ciPending and is retried first every cycle, preventing later PRs from recording CI, reviews, or merge state. Command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-pKEV2z/claude-501/review-poller.ts`. findings.title: Job reruns can also rerun downstream security tests
findings.detail: GitHub's job rerun endpoint reruns the selected job and its dependent jobs. The security checks inspect only the selected job; the sibling lookup also filters immediately to that job's name. Consequently, a permitted transient rerun can automatically rerun a downstream security job, violating the security-test exclusion.
findings.failure_scenario: A timed-out unit-test job has a dependent security-test job using `needs` and `if: always()`. Rerunning the unit-test job also reruns the security job.
